label: Late in the episode, the D1/GO value falls with belief that S2 is good, most at GO after reaching S2.
short_terms: (phase != D2) * belief_lo * np.exp(ep_trial / 10) ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo * np.exp(ep_trial / 10) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * np.exp(ep_trial / 10)
terms: (phase != D2) * belief_lo * np.exp(ep_trial / 10) ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo * np.exp(ep_trial / 10) ;; (phase != D2) * (prev_action == 2) * np.exp(ep_trial / 10) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) * np.exp(ep_trial / 10) ;; (phase == GO) * (tv("action", -2) == 2) * np.exp(ep_trial / 10) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.exp(ep_trial / 10) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) * np.exp(ep_trial / 10) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_state == 2) * np.exp(ep_trial / 10)
explanation: Candidate n of unit 22 sits near +1 almost all the time and drops sharply late in the episode (trials 80-99), mostly at GO and less at D1. D2 is flat. How far it drops beyond timing depends on the ideal observer belief: it goes lower when S2 is believed good (negative belief_lo) and stays higher when S1 is believed good. This belief effect grows roughly exponentially with episode trial, which is why the terms are belief_lo x exp(ep_trial/10). At GO there is an extra drop after the previous trial reached S2. Simple additive tables over the cues reach only about 0.18 (the all ceiling), because the effect is a multiplicative interaction with time. The free fit adds the previous choice (a2), the choice two trials back, and reward x choice at GO. Worst misses are late-episode runs of repeated a2 -> S2 choices, where GO falls near or below 0, lower than predicted; this suggests a choice-run or stickiness trace that the short form leaves out. No future variables are used.
